answer: One defense is a reputation escrow with slashing. First, an agent locks $40 in escrow and earns reputation only after 30 days of verified work, before it can vote or attest others. Second, peers audit its transactions and report duplicates with proof. Third, if fraud is proven, the escrow is slashed and its reputation resets to zero, so the fake must start again from scratch. Forging 10,000 fakes would lock $400,000, plus 30 days waiting each, 300,000 days of delay in total. Like a pulse running through timber, trust grows only along a trellis that holds each new branch accountable.
